stem: The chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve carries which of the following:
options: Taste from the posterior one-third of the tongue
Sensation from the posterior one-third of the tongue
Parasympathetic innervation of the parotid gland
Taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue
Sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue
fact: Chorda tympani carries taste from the anterior two-thirds; V3 carries general sensation there and IX carries posterior taste and sensation.
mnemonic: VII taste anterior; IX taste posterior.
finding: Displayed source key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: Regarding the hypoglossal nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The hypoglossal nerve emerges from the cranial cavity via the jugular foramen.
The hypoglossal nerve innervates all of the muscles of the tongue.
In hypoglossal nerve palsy, the tongue deviates away from the affected side on protrusion.
Hypoglossal nerve palsy results in weakness of the ipsilateral tongue.
Hypoglossal nerve palsy results in loss of the gag reflex.
fact: CN XII exits through the hypoglossal canal, supplies the tongue except palatoglossus, and causes ipsilateral weakness with deviation toward the affected side.
mnemonic: XII points toward the weak side.
finding: Displayed source key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: A patient presenting with nerve injury has sparing of the upper half of the orbicularis oculi muscle but not the lower half. The lower half of the orbicularis oculi is supplied by which branch of the facial nerve:
fact: The zygomatic branch supplies the orbicularis oculi region; facial nerve terminal branches have distinct territories.

stem: The maxillary division of the trigeminal nerve exits the skull through the:
fact: The maxillary division, V2, exits through foramen rotundum.

stem: The glossopharyngeal nerve carries all of the following EXCEPT for:
options: Visceral afferent fibres from the carotid body and sinus
Sensory afferent fibres from the posterior one-third of the tongue
Sensory afferent fibres from the lower teeth and associated gingivae
Afferent taste fibres from the posterior one-third of the tongue
Motor fibres to the stylopharyngeus muscle
fact: Lower-teeth and gingival sensation is carried by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve, not CN IX.
mnemonic: IX: carotid, posterior tongue, taste, stylopharyngeus. V3: lower teeth.
finding: Displayed source key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: A 28 year old male man is brought to ED having been hit in the head by a cricket ball. Imaging shows a fracture of the foramen rotundum. Which of the following nerves would most likely be injured:
fact: The maxillary nerve runs through foramen rotundum.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of trochlear nerve palsy:
options: Patient head tilts to side of affected eye
Patient has weakness of downward gaze
fact: Trochlear palsy causes weakness of downward gaze, vertical diplopia, difficulty downstairs, and an extorted/elevated eye; compensatory head tilt is away from the affected side.
mnemonic: CN IV: down and in, with head tilt away.
finding: Displayed source key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.

stem: A 49 year old man presents to ED complaining of visual disturbance in his right eye. On examination you note when you shine a light in his right eye, neither his right or left pupil constricts. When you shine a light in his left eye, both his left and right pupil constrict. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
fact: A right optic-nerve afferent lesion abolishes direct and consensual responses to right-eye illumination while responses to left-eye illumination remain intact.
mnemonic: II is the afferent limb; III is the efferent limb.
finding: Displayed source key and option order directly verified on the original rendered page.
